blogs.title: When One Dose Isn’t Enough: Managing Multiphasic Anaphylaxis in the ICU
blogs.description: A deep dive into the challenges of recognizing and treating multiphasic anaphylaxis, using the presented case to explore decision‑making around repeated epinephrine dosing, ICU admission criteria, and when (or if) to consider continuous IV epinephrine. The post will contrast standard biphasic protocols with the nuances of multiple relapses, offering practical algorithms for bedside clinicians.

blogs.title: Epinephrine Auto‑Injectors vs. Weight‑Based Dosing: Are We Underdosing Adults?
blogs.description: An evidence‑based critique of the 0.3 mg auto‑injector dose commonly used in adult anaphylaxis. The article will review pharmacologic rationale, recent pediatric‑adult dosing studies, and the presented case’s reliance on 0.3 mg devices, highlighting risks of under‑dosing in patients >50 kg and proposing institutional strategies to ensure adequate epinephrine delivery.

blogs.title: Corticosteroids in Anaphylaxis: Tradition vs. Modern Evidence
blogs.description: This blog will examine the historical role of systemic steroids for preventing biphasic reactions, juxtaposed with contemporary systematic reviews and the case’s extensive steroid use. It will discuss why guidelines are moving away from routine steroids, potential harms, and how clinicians can balance legacy practice with evolving data.

blogs.title: Systemic Mastocytosis as a Hidden Driver of Severe (Multi)phasic Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: An exploration of mast cell disorders—especially systemic mastocytosis—as risk factors for refractory and multiphasic anaphylaxis. Using the case’s elevated tryptase and minor WHO criteria, the post will outline diagnostic work‑up, interpretation of tryptase trends, and tailored management (e.g., prophylactic antihistamines, mast cell stabilizers) for at‑risk patients.

blogs.title: Observation Times After Anaphylaxis: How Long Is Long Enough?
blogs.description: A review of current guideline recommendations for post‑anaphylaxis monitoring, the variability in reported biphasic incidence, and the practical implications of the case’s 24‑hour ICU observation. The article will propose a risk‑stratified observation framework and discuss resource implications for busy emergency departments.

blogs.title: Designing a Registry for Rare Anaphylaxis Phenomena: From Case Reports to Consensus Guidelines
blogs.description: A forward‑looking piece on the need for a multinational anaphylaxis registry focusing on biphasic and multiphasic events. It will outline key data elements (e.g., dosing, tryptase kinetics, mast cell disease status), potential challenges, and how aggregated data could drive evidence‑based recommendations, citing the presented case as a template.
